description.narrative: The program seeks to promote an enabling environment in Nepal for the effective delivery of public goods and services, especially at the local level. It will do this by strengthening national and local linkages in public financial management (PFM), mitigating fiduciary risks through greater transparency and public participation, modernizing procurement systems, and enhancing the effectiveness of oversight and accountability agencies. The program will support efforts by the Government of Nepal to reform budget, fiscal and fiduciary risk management at the subnational or local government level (district development committee [DDC], municipality and village development committee [VDC]), public procurement, and oversight and accountability institutions at the national level. The program is aligned with ADB's Nepal country partnership strategy for 2010-2012, which seeks to enhance transparency and accountability, strengthen local governance, and increase the effectiveness of service delivery.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Indicator Indicator: Proportion of community-level projects selected through the ward citizen forums and community awareness centers increased to 33% (2011 baseline: less than 10%) Progress/Status: The proportion was 65% (out of 105,976 community-level projects) in FY2012; and 80% (out of 146,135 projects) in FY2016. Data Source: MOF reports MOFALD reports Actual value:

Output: Fiduciary risk management strengthened at the local government level. Indicator: The Chief Commissioner and commissioners of CIAA are appointed by October 2015 (baseline: positions vacant) Progress/Status: The Chief Commissioner was appointed in May 2013 and five other commissioners were appointed in April 2015. They are appointed for a term of six years. Data Source: CIAA reports NVC reports OAG reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: A medium-term budget framework at the national level for local development is in place by July 2015 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: A three-year medium-term budget framework for MOFALD has been prepared for FY2017-FY2019. Although it came into effect in FY2017 following MOF's approval on 22 August 2016, it has been disrupted by evolving federalization process including the restructuring of the local governments and passage of a federal budget for FY2018. Data Source: MOF reports MOFALD reports Baseline year: 2011 Baseline year: 2011 Target year: 2015

Output: Indicator Indicator: A pilot municipal administration and revenue system established by October 2015 (baseline: manual system) Progress/Status: The MARS has been developed, tested, and piloted in all 32 wards of in Kathmandu Metropolitan City as of end-April 2017. Data Source: Local Bodies Fiscal Commission reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Compliance rate of taxpayers in MARS pilot municipality increases (baseline: 30%) Progress/Status: However, due to the delay in piloting the MARS (largely caused by the disruption caused by the 2015 earthquake and the subsequent prolonged trade and transit disruption), and the disruption in the effective operation of MARS due to the local elections and establishment of new local governments in May/June 2017, progress on tax compliance is not yet evident. Data Source: MOF reports MOFALD reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Comprehensive reporting system of fiscal transfers established, including data on disbursement of funding for GESI activities as per block grant guidelines for local government bodies—i.e., 15% for disadvantaged groups, 10% for women, and 10% for children by July 2015 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: MOFALD and LBFC have established an effective system of allocating grants to local governments based on the MCPM system, including a system of MCPM assessment, computation of grant amounts based on performance, and proper recording of the grants allocated and disbursed to the local governments. However, this system will now need to be revamped and adapted to the new federal structure the country is transition to. Data Source: Local Bodies Fiscal Commission reports Baseline year: 2011 Baseline year: 2011 Target year: 2015
Output: Indicator Indicator: More VDCs are regularly subject to internal audit (baseline: none) Progress/Status: Data not available. Data Source: MOF reports MOFALD reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Number of DDC and VDC staff trained in basic accounting and internal audit increases (baseline: none) Progress/Status: About 1,634 DDC and VDC staff were trained as of FY2015. Data Source: MOF reports MOFALD reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Number of DDC and municipality staff trained in applying the Procurement Act and Regulation grows by July 2014 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: About 1500 staffs of DDC and municipalities have been trained by PPMO. Data Source: PPMO reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Performance guidelines and measures (including GESI indicators) developed for allocating block grants to VDCs by July 2013 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: MC-PM guidelines for DDCs, municipalities, and VDCs were revised in September 2013, incorporating PM indicator on budget allocation and expenditure on GESI activities. However, this system will need to be adapted to the needs of the new federal system. Data Source: Local Bodies Fiscal Commission reports Baseline year: 2011 Baseline year: 2011 Target year: 2013

Output: Indicator Indicator: Procurement plans of ministries published electronically by July 2015 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: All ministries prepared procurement plans but information is not yet available as to how many ministries published electronically. Data Source: PPMO reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Procurement plans prepared for DDCs and municipalities by July 2014 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: 72 DDCs (96%) and 146 municipalities (67%) prepared procurement plans in FY2016. Data Source: PPMO reports

Output: Indicator Indicator: Software for e-government procurement is developed by October 2014 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: Development of software for e-procurement was completed in July 2015. Data Source: PPMO reports

Output: Local government budget and fiscal management improved Indicator: Complaints response system is established in the NVC by July 2014 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: The Complaint Management System has been established and strengthened in 2014, by introducing a procedure for screening of complaints by an oversight committee within NVC. NVC also started developing an automated complaints recording system. Data Source: CIAA reports NVC reports OAG reports

Output: Public procurement system enhanced. Indicator: Proportion of senior civil servants who comply with asset declaration grows by July 2014 (baseline: 63% in July 2011) Progress/Status: 93.26% of the staffs and officials who are required to submit assets declaration declared their assets in FY2015. This was an increment of 37,327 asset declarations (about 10%) from the previous years. Data Source: CIAA reports NVC reports OAG reports
The efficiency, transparency, and integrity of Nepal?s public finances at the national and local government levels are enhanced.

The proportion of government procurement entities that use the e-GP system reaches 25% by November 2015 (2011 baseline: 0%) Progress/Status: As of 15 September 2017, about 1,100 procurement entities were using the e-GP system. It is now madatory for all contracts exceeding NRs 6 million (equivalent US$ 60,000) to use the e-GP system and contracts exceeding NRs 20 million(equivalent US$200,000) to use 1S2E procedure of the e-GP system. Data Source: PPMO reports Actual value:

Amount of disallowed funds by auditor-general recovered by government grows by July 2015 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: The recovery rate was 66.8%, 49%, and 52.8% in FY2014, FY2015, and FY2016, respectively. Data for FY2017 not yet available. Data Source: OAG reports

Annual audit reports of local government bodies are published electronically by October 2015 (baseline: none) Progress/Status: The Office of the Auditor General publishes audit reports of DDCs in its website.. Data Source: MOFALD reports
